method: Read criteria, inspect 12 supplied public UI captures and generation code independently, then review paired report. No app mutation or new browser/window.

independentFindings.finding: Large named Gaegyeong city does contain dwellings, market stalls, people, gate, wall and nearby fields. Byeokrando viewpoint sees much of the same city; the inspected scene does not communicate harbor work. Symbolic repetition alone is not an error; city footprints and terrain fit need separate checking.

Ganghwa city and Tripitaka carving share effectively the same area anchor. Event-first ordering compacts the later city to a primary hall only, consistent with the 1240 capture. City existence and local temporary activity are coupled.

Jikji sponsor Myodeok is marked on-site; publication actors are assigned working. Existing institution text establishes sponsorship, not being physically at the printing table. Nonappearance is not established either.

Global year selects Goryeo building and figure family; buildingArchetype ignores regional information beyond seed. The 920 Silla capital can therefore use the Goryeo family while retaining its Silla label. This proves a time/region selection limitation, not that all historical Korean housing had to look different.

Pyongyang and Gangjin inspected views show anonymous houses, fields and paths but no named regional activity. Camera targets do not prove historical site coordinates or all-data absence. Sanggyong target z=-899.17 lies beyond worldBounds.minZ=-720.10; blank view is not evidence that Balhae has no historical records.

The named Tripitaka carving workforce is a Polity/group entity. Context.people and visible participants filter to Person. Publication composition adds no anonymous labor figures, so a source-backed group can stay in side metadata without producing carving workers. A helper probe misclassifies the words daejangdogam as commander, but that helper output is NOT evidence of a visible commander in this scene.
